articles.title: Explained: Why two Republic of Ireland vs Israel matches have become so controversial
articles.summary: The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.
articles.body:
Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror .

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June , while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium .

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times .">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions . A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters . "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC , that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest .

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press , Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

articles.title: Tyson Fury to face British rival Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11
articles.summary: The fight, one of the biggest in British boxing history, will be broadcast on streaming service Netflix.
articles.body:
Tyson Fury will face Anthony Joshua in an all-British heavyweight showdown in Cardiff on December 11.

The long-awaited clash had initially been linked with venues in New York and London before promoters settled on the Principality Stadium in the Welsh capital.

After months of negotiations that threatened to scupper the fight, as Fury called for a rematch with Oleksandr Usyk , Saudi Arabian boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh announced the venue and date for the bout on Thursday.

“For 15 years no one has been able to make this fight,” he wrote on social media.

“Back in April, I said that any announcement would come from me. I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. The time for talking is over…”

Choosing the 80,000-capacity stadium in Cardiff, which has hosted the Champions League and FA Cup finals, as well as Wales national team matches in football and rugby, allows both fighters to finally start their preparations for the eagerly anticipated clash.

The fight, one of the biggest in British boxing history, will be broadcast on streaming service Netflix.

Fury, 37, defeated 46-year-old Mariusz Wach in Thailand in his most recent bout in July.

Joshua, 36, survived a pair of first-round knockdowns to beat the unheralded Kristian Prenga in his last fight two months ago.

articles.title: Emily Fox makes 'easy decision' to sign new contract at Arsenal
articles.summary: USA international Emily Fox has described signed a new contract at Arsenal as "an easy decision".
articles.body:
USA international Emily Fox has described her decision to sign a new contract at Arsenal as "an easy decision".

The 28-year-old has been a key player for the club since joining from North Carolina Courage in 2024 and is understood to have signed a new three-year deal.

She was part of the squad that won the Women's Champions League title in 2025 and the Women's Champions Cup trophy in 2026.

In her first season at the club, she won the Women's League Cup and has been named in the PFA team of the year in the last two campaigns.

Speaking to BBC Sport, she said: "I'm very pleased to be able to continue my journey with Arsenal and it was honestly an easy decision because of where I want to be now, and in a few years' time.

"When I think of how I'm going to grow, be challenged and be in an environment where it's like my second home, I think of Arsenal.

"It is a club that is wanting to continue to push the women's game, invest in it and focus on the community, the history of it, the culture, and wanting to excel."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

BBC Sport reported in January that Fox had a year remaining on her existing contract but Arsenal were always confident she would stay at the club.

She has established herself as one of the best full-backs in the world and has made almost 100 appearances for Arsenal in all competitions.

However, despite helping Renee Slegers' side to European glory in 2025, Fox feels there is one important medal missing from her collection - the WSL title.

"There is definitely some unfinished business. We want to keep going, keep winning and maybe get some things that we've already won before too," said Fox.

"Being at Arsenal, there's always going to be high expectations from the inside and the outside. That's just part of it.

"When you have big goals like that, you have to take it game-by-game and you can't look too far ahead. That's my approach."

Fox is also preparing for a big summer with the USA, under the management of ex-Chelsea boss Emma Hayes, as they hope to go far at the 2027 Women's World Cup.

"We're starting off strong by playing Spain twice at home in October. This year has been great for us in terms of the opponents and the challenges," she added.

"I feel like we've played a lot of variety with our opponents and it's given us a taste of different environments, different tactics and layers of how we're going to play.

"That's ultimately what you need to do when you want to win a World Cup. In November, we have to qualify. Those are our objectives."

articles.title: Aubameyang, operado con éxito de la rodilla derecha
articles.standfirst: Ha pasado por el quirófano esta mañana en una clínica de Madrid
articles.summary: Ha pasado por el quirófano esta mañana en una clínica de Madrid
articles.body: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ha sido intervenido con éxito esta mañana de su rodilla derecha por el traumatólogo Manuel Leyes en el Centro Olympia de Madrid. El jugador del Deportivo ha pasado por el quirófano para solventar las molestias en el menisco externo de su rodilla derecha que sufrió durante el partido contra el Betis. El delantero, que ya ha recibido el alta hospitalaria, regresará a A Coruña para iniciar su proceso de recuperación. "Su evolución marcará su regreso a los entrenamientos con el grupo", se lee en el comunicado del club sobre el tiempo que estará de baja. No obstante, lo más probable es que Aubameyang esté ausente entre cuatro y seis semanas. La baja del atacante se une a la de Marc Casadó, que también estará lesionado unos tres meses. Son dos futbolistas importantes con los que no podrá contar el entrenador Antonio Hidalgo. "El Dépor va a seguir bien, están listos. Yo confío", decía el delantero sobre su ausencia a su salida del hospital, en declaraciones recogidas por Carrusel Deportivo. Aubameyang, de 37 años, atravesaba por un momento de forma espectacular. A pesar de la edad, había comenzado la temporada a pleno rendimiento y había marcado cinco goles, además de dar dos asistencias.

articles.title: Kubo juega y gana con Japón
articles.standfirst: El atacante de la Real ha sido uno de los primeros futbolistas a los que el seleccionador nipón ha dado entrada con 1-1 contra Uruguay y ha conseguido ganar por 3-1
articles.summary: El atacante de la Real ha sido uno de los primeros futbolistas a los que el seleccionador nipón ha dado entrada con 1-1 contra Uruguay y ha conseguido ganar por 3-1
articles.body: Take Kubo atraviesa por su peor momento en la Real Sociedad, con la que ha sido suplente en los cuatro partidos más recientes y no tuvo minutos en dos, como reflejamos el martes pasado en MARCA, por lo que salir de revulsivo y lograr la victoria, como ha hecho hoy con Japón ante Uruguay, le puede venir bien para su moral. Kubo ha vuelto a ser reserva con su selección, en el amistoso que ha jugado contra Uruguay, pero se incorporó más tarde y pese a realizar sólo un entrenamiento o dos el seleccionador, con 1-1 en el electrónico, ha echado mano de él para un cuadruple cambio en el minuto 64 que ha resultado decisivo, al terminar venciendo los nipones por 3-1, aunque el txuriurdin no ha podido colaborar con algún gol o asistencia.

articles.title: Women's Champions League: What we learned from return of Europe's top tier competition
articles.summary: Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City start bids for European glory in unconvincing fashion.
articles.body:
The Women's Champions League returned this week and with it came a host of unanswered questions for the ambitious English trio involved.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City all have designs on winning the competition and, on the face of it, got their campaigns off to solid starts.

Arsenal and Chelsea both have three points after narrow home wins while City recovered from 2-0 down for a creditable draw at heavyweights Bayern Munich.

But scratch deeper, and this was an unconvincing week, particularly given last season's finalists Barcelona and Lyon both opened with commanding victories.

Are the Women's Super League clubs equipped to challenge this season? What still needs addressing? And who has the best chance of lifting the trophy in Warsaw next May?

Last season, Manchester City exploited their absence from European competition to romp to the Women's Super League title.

In returning to the elite tier this season, their squad will face greater tests, and that was immediately true when 2025-26 semi-finalists Bayern Munich raced into a two-goal lead.

But Andree Jeglertz's team gave an immediate indication they belong at this level by recovering to draw 2-2, with summer signings Beth Mead and Carlotta Wamser justifying their arrival at the champions with their first goals for the club.

That was crucial given usual goalscorer Khadija Shaw surprisingly proved fallible in missing a penalty.

When she inevitably finds her shooting boots, City should be just fine in this competition.

Man City fight back from two down to thwart Bayern

With only two goals and five points from three matches, it has been an inauspicious start to the season for Arsenal, who have been bullish in targeting trophies.

Up against Danish minnows HB Koge, it was not just the Disney+ TV coverage of the game that was marred by glitches.

Arsenal's expected goals tally of 1.93 does not tell the story of a performance that was dominant with the ball, but they only fashioned two shots on target against a side they were expected to beat comfortably.

Boss Renee Slegers made a raft of changes, including resting Alessia Russo, but the eight forwards she ultimately featured struggled to breach the resolute visitors' backline, with the Gunners requiring a 95th-minute penalty to steal the points.

Dismissing lower-ranked teams at the start of competition has been an Achilles' heel for Arsenal and, while they did win, tougher tests await and Slegers needs to find a solution.

Ad break in Women's Champions League was unscheduled

Wasteful Arsenal need late penalty to beat Koge

A brilliant goal from Wieke Kaptein handed Chelsea victory on their opening night in what was a promising attacking performance from the Blues.

Summer signing Melvine Malard was bright in her pre-planned 45-minute appearance, while Alyssa Thompson's electric display showcased what she could offer in her second season at Stamford Bridge.

With Ellie Carpenter playing behind Thompson, Chelsea's right side could be a potent weapon as they strive to return to the summit of English football - and, in reality, they ought to have added a couple more goals against Austria Vienna.

However, there were concerns for Sonia Bompastor. Shorn of injured captain Erin Cuthbert and with Keira Walsh substituted early, they ceded control in midfield to the Champions League debutants.

Indeed, Vienna came close on a number of occasions to taking a deserved point, hitting the post and having more shots than their esteemed opponents.

Although Chelsea have only conceded one goal in four matches this season, the fragility on display could cost them against more clinical opponents.

Chelsea win Champions League opener but Walsh injured

As English clubs stuttered through their first games, last season's finalists Barcelona and Lyon both made a statement.

First to play were the French giants at Servette in Switzerland, where they won 8-0, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring a hat-trick as they racked up 31 shots and hit the woodwork.

Holders Barcelona actually went behind at home to Paris FC but swiftly turned the game around and scored four before half-time, ultimately running out 5-2 winners.

Ominous signs from the Champions League favourites.

articles.title: Premier League Bermuda Triangle: Do stats back Brighton, Bournemouth, Brentford social media theory?
articles.summary: Do the stats back the social media meme that Bournemouth, Brighton and Brentford form a Premier League 'Bermuda Triangle' where teams lose points?
articles.body:
It's the place where points are lost and never to be seen again, according to a popular social media meme.

Draw a line from Brighton to Bournemouth to Brentford and back down to Brighton again and you will have formed the Premier League's very own "Bermuda Triangle".

Those three clubs have developed a reputation for taking points off the traditional Big Six - Arsenal , Chelsea , Liverpool , Manchester City , Manchester United and Tottenham .

Recent results have only fuelled the narrative and helped to push the tongue-in-cheek theory.

On Friday night, Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0 . Less than 24 hours later, B righton outclassed champions Arsenal , albeit by the same scoreline - though it was a victory that could arguably have been even more emphatic had David Raya not produced a couple of smart saves.

Bournemouth , meanwhile, pushed Liverpool all the way before falling to a gritty 1-0 defeat, with Alisson forced into a brilliant recovery stop to deny the Cherries an early opener.

Those are the sort of performances that stick in supporters' minds and help explain why the theory has taken hold.

Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Brighton have been the best-performing non-traditional Big Six side against Arsenal , Chelsea , Liverpool , Man City, Manchester United and Spurs, taking 42 points from 26 games - an average of 1.62 points per match.

The Cherries are not far behind, collecting 35 points from 26 matches, or 1.35 points per game.

Brentford , however, have taken 22 points from 26 matches, averaging 0.85 points per game. Newcastle (1.46), Nottingham Forest (1.46) and Aston Villa (1.38) have all matched or outperformed the Bees against the traditional Big Six over the same period.

In other words, the clubs most commonly grouped together by the meme have produced very different levels of success against elite opposition.

Brighton and Bournemouth have consistently taken points off the Premier League's heavyweights. Brentford 's record is less convincing.

In fact, the Opta data suggests Brighton are the main reason the theory has gained such traction.

Since Fabian Hurzeler took charge, only Kenny Dalglish's Blackburn have recorded a better points-per-game return against the traditional Big Six among managers of non-Big-Six clubs with at least 10 matches.

The popularity of the Bermuda Triangle idea may say as much about perception as results.

When it comes to recruitment and spending, Bournemouth , Brighton and Brentford operate in a different world to the Premier League's biggest clubs. They cannot simply outspend Arsenal , Liverpool or Manchester City .

That makes their victories more memorable. Upsets also tend to linger longer in the memory because they fit a familiar story: well-run clubs outperforming opponents with significantly greater resources.

The meme is not entirely without foundation, although the evidence is considerably stronger for Brighton and Bournemouth than it is for Brentford .

Brentford 's overall record is weaker, although a series of eye-catching victories under Thomas Frank and now Keith Andrews have helped cement their reputation as a difficult opponent for elite clubs. And the start to this season has helped: their Chelsea success added to by an opening day 3-0 rout of Spurs .

But the numbers do not support a three-club phenomenon quite as clearly as social media might suggest.

If there is a Premier League Bermuda Triangle, Brighton sit firmly at its centre.

The Seagulls' record against the traditional Big Six is not merely impressive by modern standards. According to Opta, it is one of the best any non-Big-Six club has produced in the Premier League era.

The only catch is that the evidence points less to a triangle and more to one standout club, with Bournemouth providing strong support and Brentford helping to supply some of the moments that keep the theory alive.

articles.title: Valles se pone en la piel de Luis De la Fuente: "Hay muchos y muy buenos porteros españoles..."
articles.standfirst: El portero del Betis analiza en Radio MARCA su gran momento y su ausencia en la lista de la Selección
articles.summary: El portero del Betis analiza en Radio MARCA su gran momento y su ausencia en la lista de la Selección
articles.body: Una de las claves del gran arranque de temporada del Betis, con 16 puntos de 21 posibles en LaLiga y con un triunfo en su primer partido de la Champions, está en la portería. Álvaro Valles se ha consolidado como guardameta titular indiscutible para Pellegrini y sus registros, convertido en el portero con más paradas de las cinco grandes ligas europeas, le avalan. Así ha valorado este inicio de campeonato el de La Rinconada en una entrevista en Radio MARCA Sevilla en la que entiende el difícil papel de Luis de la Fuente a la hora de elegir portero para la Selección. Gran arranque personal y del equipo: "Sí, por supuesto. Al final creo que va también unido una cosa con la otra. Creo que si el equipo está dando un rendimiento bueno y alto, pues también es más fácil que uno personalmente esté dando un buen rendimiento y te contagie el nivel de los compañeros." Su buen momento de forma: "Sí, la verdad es que sí. Después de ese año en blanco que tuve, fue una temporada complicada para mí en el sentido de que yo era consciente en todo momento, sobre todo al principio de iLga, de que no estaba en mi mejor nivel, aunque estuviera haciendo todo lo posible para ello. Por suerte, poco a poco y con el paso de los partidos pude ir de manera ascendente. Este año creo que estoy dando mi mejor nivel también porque, como has dicho antes, en lo colectivo el equipo está dando un nivel muy alto." Superar la inactividad: "Sí, está claro. Al final, cuando uno vuelve de las vacaciones de verano tiene que volver a retomar ese 'timing' y tener la distancia cogida. Imagínate después de un año prácticamente sin poder competir...". Trabajo físico de grupo e individual: "Sí, es verdad que este año desde la pretemporada nos hemos enfocado mucho más en el tema del gimnasio y del entrenamiento personal. La verdad es que cuando tocas algo y haces algo distinto o le pones más énfasis a algo que el año anterior no hacías y encima te está dando resultado, pues es mucho más fácil." Volumen ofensivo y seguridad atrás: "Sí, es verdad que el equipo genera mucho en ataque y creo que se ha podido estar más acertado, pero creo que lo importante es también generar esas ocasiones. La tranquilidad que te da es que el equipo siempre sabe de sobra que va a generar y que alguna va a entrar. Por eso la importancia de mantener los máximos partidos posibles la portería a cero, porque es raro el partido en el que el equipo no hace algún gol". Victorias por la mínima: "Al final, cuando no las materializas, intentas ayudar al equipo desde atrás lo mejor posible, sabiendo que si no encajas gol, con esa ventaja es suficiente como para ganar el partido". Ilusión por la Champions: "Sí, la ilusión es tremenda. Es verdad que, partido a partido, en Champions cualquier equipo te puede ganar porque es la máxima competición y si el equipo rival contra el que juegas está en Champions es porque es un gran equipo y tiene argumentos para ganarte. Pero sí, la ilusión está ahí. Creo que el equipo hizo un primer partido muy bueno sacando los tres puntos fuera de casa, que eso es importantísimo. Nuestra ilusión y nuestro objetivo es estar dentro de esos 24 equipos y poder seguir avanzando en esta Champions". Calidad de la plantilla: "Sí, por supuesto. Creo que tenemos un plantel muy bueno y sobre todo creo que todos los jugadores estamos dando un rendimiento muy alto, lo que hace que la alternancia en el once inicial se note lo menos posible. Todo el que sale del banquillo o de inicio, independientemente de quién sea, está dando un nivel muy alto y lo está haciendo bien". Margen de mejora e integración del vestuario: "Pensamos que tenemos un gran equipo, muy completo, en el que el que sale en el once inicial lo va a hacer igual de bien que el que ha salido en el anterior. Eso es lo importante: que tenemos esa confianza todos en todos y sabemos que los 25 ó 27 jugadores que estamos todos los días, juegue uno o juegue otro, van a dar un rendimiento muy alto. Lo más importante es esa unión y ver que todos los jugadores están a su máximo nivel o dando lo máximo que tienen, lo que hace mejorar al compañero". Convocatoria de Josep Martínez y la Selección: "No me ha sorprendido porque lo conozco bastante bien. Sé que es un gran portero y que este es el primer año que le han dado la oportunidad de defender la portería del Inter de Milán, un equipo histórico en el fútbol europeo y mundial, y estoy muy contento por él. Tengo muy buena relación con él desde hace bastantes años y me alegro bastante de que pueda estar en la Selección y pueda disfrutar de ello, porque creo que también se lo merece". Sus números son mejores: "Lo de si los números son mejores o peores que los míos son cosas que tienen que ver los seleccionadores. Yo sigo contento y feliz. Me alegro de que lo llamen a la Selección porque es un magnífico portero y una persona increíble. Yo voy a seguir trabajando, muy contento por darle a mi club lo que necesita y poder ayudar cada partido lo máximo posible; ese es el nivel que tengo que mantener toda la temporada. Lo de la selección llegará o no, pero creo que lo importante es tener esa regularidad, poder ayudar a mi club lo máximo posible y darle la máxima alegría posible a la afición". Competencia en la portería para De la Fuente: "Es la suerte que tiene España y la mala suerte que tenemos los porteros: hay muchos y muy buenos porteros españoles. Creo que el nivel es bastante bueno y es complicado quitar a otro compañero de la portería de la Selección, porque son grandes porteros". Referentes bajo palos: "Cuando era más pequeño tuve la suerte de poder ver a Iker Casillas, que creo que para todo portero español que haya estado en esa época ha sido uno de sus referentes. Al final creo que ha sido uno de los mejores porteros del mundo y de la historia de España e internacionalmente, ha dado mucho. También he vivido la época de Buffon y luego, con el cambio de juego en el fútbol y esa revolución del juego de toque y de los pies, me he fijado mucho siempre en Neuer, Ter Stegen y actualmente pienso que el mejor portero del mundo, el más completo, es Thibaut Courtois. Creo que difícilmente vamos a ver a un portero que dé un nivel como el que ha dado Thibaut". Días de descanso y vida personal: ""Sí, yo soy casero. Es verdad que nos gusta irnos por ahí a la familia, pero ahora con el colegio, los niños y demás es más complicado. Nos gusta irnos al pueblo y estar tranquilos allí, disfrutar de la familia y de los amigos".

articles.title: Alessandro Romano: Suiza podría reclamarle ¡100.000 euros! a Italia por el 'robo' del 'nuovo' Rodri
articles.standfirst: El medio del Cagliari formaba parte de un programa especial de captación de talentos de la Federación helvética
articles.summary: El medio del Cagliari formaba parte de un programa especial de captación de talentos de la Federación helvética
articles.body: Resulta difícil imaginar un nombre más italiano que el de Alessandro Gianni Romano (Winterthur, 17-6-2006). Pues, por increíble que parezca, Italia se lo ha robado a Suiza. Es más, según 'La Gazzetta dello Sport', la Federación helvética no descarta reclamarle 100.000 euros a la 'Azzurra' en concepto de daños y perjuicios. Y es que el ahora mediocampista del Cagliari formaba parte de un programa especial ('Footuro') a través del que la 'ASF' selecciona a los talentos más prometedores y les somete a un entrenamiento específico. Sin embargo, tras ser capitán e internacional con Suiza en categorías inferiores hasta en 34 ocasiones, Romano jugará con Italia. Los viajes a Cerdeña de Murat Yakin para convencerle de que sería el 'nuevo Xhaka' fueron en vano. "Hablé con mi familia y tomé una decisión con el corazón. Sentía que mi camino tenía que estar en Italia. Pero no fue una decisión en contra de Suiza, un país al que estoy muy agradecido: viviendo allí, crecí como persona y aprendí cinco idiomas (suizo, alemán, francés, inglés e italiano). Fue mi deseo de ir a Italia lo que me convenció", confiesa. Un cambio de nacionalidad que puede tener premio. 'Il Rodri azzurro', como ya le ha bautizado 'La Gazzetta', apunta a titular contra Bélgica en la Nations League. "Todo pasó tan rápido que todavía no me lo creo. Trabajé muy duro para merecer una oportunidad en las grandes ligas, pero nunca imaginé que la Serie A y la selección llegarían tan pronto", reconocía a 'Raisport'. "Es increíble. De niño veía al entrenador por televisión, cuando ganaba la Eurocopa, y ahora puedo hablar con él; tengo su número de teléfono", insiste Romano, que no duda en admitir que le debe "mucho" a Claudio Ranieri. El ahora director técnico de la 'Nazionale' le dio la oportunidad de subir a entrenar con el primer equipo de la Roma. Una Roma que, al igual que Suiza, debe estar tirándose de los pelos. Le envió cedido al Cagliari con una opción de compra obligatoria -no hay opción de recompra- valorada en 5 millones de euros. "Fue una decisión del club y del entrenador. No me molestó. De hecho, estoy contento en Cagliari. Claramente, éste era mi camino", señala. Ahora Inter, Juventus y Milan siguen de cerca al segundo mediocampista de la Serie A que más disparos a puerta realiza (5 de 7), el tercero que más 'tackles' (entradas) realiza (9 de 11), el décimo que más centros completa con éxito (4 de 11) y el 11º que más recuperaciones efectúa (23). Todo ello con un 88,23% de acierto en el pase (195/221). "Mi punto fuerte, si se me permite decirlo, es la técnica. Desde pequeño trabajé mucho con mi padre, y luego intento hacer ambas fases, con y sin balón, lo mejor posible. Lo doy todo", incide Alessandro Romano. Y es que su padre, Umberto, ahora entrenador del juvenil del Zúrich, fue futbolista, al igual que su hermano Luca, que milita en el SC Kriens, de la Segunda suiza. Lo del 'Rodri azzurro' no es casual. "Intento admirar a todos los que juegan en mi posición y, aunque no tengo un ídolo en particular, se aprende mucho de un campeón como Rodri". En Italia confían en haber encontrado un centrocampista... para rato.

articles.title: Drinking at football matches - would fans welcome it?
articles.summary: Andy Burnham has long championed a repeal of the ban which prevents football supporters from drinking alcohol in the view of the pitch. But do fans even want it?
articles.body:
When UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham embarked on his trip to the United Nations in New York, he might not have been expecting a question about football fans drinking alcohol in grounds.

Burnham firmly believes the law that prevents supporters from having a beer at their seat during a match is outdated.

It's a position the Everton supporter has long held, and when asked was happy to reaffirm.

"I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination," said Burnham, who feels football fans are singled out compared to those of other sports and events.

There is no suggestion this is about to become official government policy, and last year MPs rejected a Conservative amendment to the Football Governance Bill that would have forced ministers to launch a formal consultation on scrapping the rule.

That was, of course, before Burnham returned to Downing Street.

It is a complicated and divisive issue, about not just safety. But is it something that match-going supporters actually want?

Drinking alcohol at football grounds in England and Wales has been strictly controlled since the Sporting Events Control of Alcohol Act was introduced in 1985.

It was brought in to counter escalating hooliganism through the 1970s and into the 1980s.

The ban impacts clubs in the Premier League down to the National League. While beer can be sold, it must be consumed in areas that do not have a view of the pitch.

Yet fans who support teams in the National League North and South and below can drink alcohol around the pitch.

The ban is more strict in Scotland, with a law in place since 1981 that alcohol is only available in hospitality areas and not for other fans.

It was initially imposed following a riot during the 1980 Scottish Cup final between Rangers and Celtic at Hampden.

However, attitudes have been changing in recent seasons.

It was lifted as part of a pilot scheme last year, with several Scottish clubs selling alcohol in clearly defined, monitored areas of the stadiums. It started with lower-level clubs, eventually being extended to the Premiership.

The Scotland national team joined the trial for the friendlies against Japan and Curacao earlier this year. It has been extended to games against Switzerland on 29 September and Slovenia next month.

The Women's Super League in England has just completed two seasons of successful trials and the rule preventing drinking in the stands has now been removed by the league's governing company, WSL Football.

The women's game is not governed by the Sporting Events Control of Alcohol Act, enabling the competition organiser to make the change.

Is there support for the move within English football's corridors of power?

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said in August the competition had not "got a specific view" and "we'd need to give it some really careful thought".

The English Football League, however, issued a statement on Thursday that said it would be "receptive to discussions around reviewing the current legislation".

It added member clubs had already provided "a mandate to lobby for appropriate reform" which had "not kept pace with significant developments in stadium management, safety and stewarding".

Fans' views differ on drinking in stands

The Football Supporters' Association has for some time backed changing the law.

Like the prime minister, it considers it to be unfair on football fans.

"I think it is outdated," FSA chairman Tom Greatrex told the BBC Radio 4 Today programme.

"If you go to watch football in Germany or in other places around the world, then it's perfectly acceptable.

"It is civilised and appropriate. There's no reason why that shouldn't be the case for football fans, as it is for fans of rugby league, watching Oasis, or anything else that happens often in the same stadiums in the same seats."

The FSA's position is that clubs should have the choice, in consultation with supporters, to sell alcohol.

Clubs might want to offer it in all stands, others in designated areas, while a few might choose not to do so at all.

Other sports offer designated alcohol-free sections, something that football clubs may wish to copy for some families and supporters who do not consume alcohol because of their religion.

The FSA acknowledges this, but believes having the option to make such decisions is important.

It believes relaxing the law would be more popular the further down the leagues you go, where alcohol sales could potentially provide a crucial additional income stream.

The UK Football Policing Unit rejected the suggestion, arguing alcohol plays "a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour" and that "other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour" that football does.

Yet for Greatrex, there is already proof police are not open to ideas through their previous opposition to safe standing.

Before it was introduced four years ago, Mark Roberts, who has been the national lead for football policing since 2014, told the BBC it would make it "easier to throw missiles, engage in hate chanting, racism, sneak alcohol in, take cocaine" .

"[The police] were telling everybody that we couldn't have standing at football again, that it would jeopardise safety, " Greatrex said.

"Actually, what we saw then was a controlled, managed pilot projects to get that re-established.

"There hasn't been the level of disorder that some of the police sources were saying there would be. I think the police should have more of an open mind and engage in this in a sensible and mature way."

For many match-going fans, however, the prospect of beer being thrown and potential anti-social behaviour outweighs the opportunity to watch a game with a pint.

Dave, a Chelsea fan from Twickenham, told Nicky Campbell on BBC Radio 5 Live, that he was "100% against it".

"Have a look at some of the footage you see on social media at Boxpark, for instance. A goal goes in and there is beer and lager thrown everywhere," he said.

"I don't want to go round stinking of other people's beer and there is a fashion among certain supporters to throw their beer everywhere.

"If people can't go without drink for a 45-minute period there is something the matter with them."

Adrian, from Leicester, claimed it would be the "worst idea you could come up with".

"There is enough trouble with other things in football, with the flares, drug taking and other things," he added. "You throw the alcohol in as well. Football is tribal whereas other sports they aren't."

But Ryan, a Wolves fan in Banbury, said "a solution that suits everybody" is to provide designated areas for drinking in stands.

What is it like in other sports and different countries?

Football is in the only sport in the UK which faces restrictions on the consumption of alcohol.

Some of these sports have issues with alcohol-related and anti-social behaviour, but none have the same reputation as football.

There is a strict ban in the top two divisions of Spanish football, where only alcohol-free beer can be sold outside of hospitality areas. It can, however, be taken to seats.

In the German Bundesliga, there is no ban on drinking at your seat. So relaxed is the approach to alcohol at games that you will even find people selling bottles of beer from shopping trolleys outside grounds.

In the Italian Serie A it is similarly as relaxed, though to a limit of 5% ABV. Some games which are designated "high risk" have sales suspended in and around the stadium.

In France, the Evin Law was introduced in 1991 which is pretty much in line with Scotland, as far as football is concerned. Alcohol cannot be sold at any sports event, other than in VIP areas.

articles.title: Rogers: "Ronaldo es mi favorito, pero jugué contra Messi en la semifinal del Mundial con 39 años..."
articles.standfirst: El futbolista del Chelsea se deshace en elogios hacia el astro argentino
articles.summary: El futbolista del Chelsea se deshace en elogios hacia el astro argentino
articles.body: Morgan Rogers, por el que este verano el Chelsea ha pagado 138 millones de euros para ficharlo procedente del Aston Villa, no olvida la exhibición de Leo Messi ante Inglaterra en la semifinal del pasado Mundial. El inglés, protagonista esta semana en el programa 'CFC Unlocked', que se emite en los canales del Chelsea, se refirió a su futbolista favorito. "Ronaldo es mi favorito personalmente, pero jugué contra Messi en la semifinal del Mundial con 39 años y no lo podía creer, no puedo imaginar como sería en su mejor momento. Puedo imaginar que en su mejor no tenías nada que hacer contra él. ¡Fue casi imposible hacer algo en este partido y tiene 39!", señaló Rogers. En aquel encuentro, Inglaterra se adelantó por medio de Gordon, a pase precisamente de Rogers. Después, en un gran segundo tiempo de Argentina en general y de Messi en particular, la Albicelteste le dio la vuelta con goles de Enzo Fernández y Lautaro, ambos a pase del '10'. Un partido que en Argentina no olvidan, por la rivalidad histórica con Inglaterra, y parece que tampoco lo hacen los ingleses. Al menos, Morgan Rogers.

articles.title: Why are Ireland vs Israel football matches so controversial?
articles.summary: Ireland and Israel will play two football matches despite growing Irish calls for a boycott due to the genocide in Gaza.
articles.body:
When European football’s governing body announced the schedule for its upcoming Nations League competition in February, one fixture became an instant point of contention.

The Republic of Ireland and Israel were allocated the same group in League B of the UEFA Nations League 2026-27 , provoking strong opposition from Irish fans, footballers and celebrities due to Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza. It also led to calls for a boycott of the fixture regardless of the consequences.

Seven months on, the Ireland vs Israel game is expected to be played as scheduled but amid vociferous criticism, louder calls for Irish football officials not to send a team to the game and bitter Israeli responses to the backlash.

What’s happening between Ireland and Israel?

They will play two matches in the space of eight days amid tense political relations and in the face of increasing opposition from the Irish public.

The fixtures will be played on a home-and-away basis, with Ireland “hosting” its home leg in Debrecen, Hungary, on Sunday, September 27. Israel’s “home” match will be played in Serbia on October 4.

Why does Ireland have to play against Israel?

Ireland and Israel are members of UEFA, European football’s governing body. As UEFA members, and in order to progress to the top tier of European football competitions and improve their rankings in international football, both nations participate in UEFA-run tournaments.

The UEFA Nations League pits closely ranked nations against each other in groups, where all teams face each other twice in round-robin-style matches.

Ireland and Israel were drawn together in Group B3 along with Austria and Kosovo.

Who is leading the calls to boycott the Ireland vs Israel match?

Ever since the fixture was first confirmed on February 12, the Football Association of Ireland has been under pressure to boycott the matches due to Israel’s genocide in Gaza and Ireland’s status as a Palestine ally.

In May, leading Irish footballers joined celebrities in a campaign by Irish Sport for Palestine, urging Ireland to boycott the match against Israel. A United Nations inquiry confirmed in June 2025 that Israel was committing a genocide in Gaza .

The campaign group says Israel has breached UEFA and FIFA statutes by allowing teams to play on occupied Palestinian land and should be stripped of its membership at both football bodies.

Last November, 93 percent of FAI members voted for its leadership to pressure UEFA to suspend Israel under those statutes, a mandate campaigners say the Irish governing body should “respect and represent”.

The letter, entitled “Stop the Game”, was signed by League of Ireland players, former men’s coach Brian Kerr and twice women’s player of the year Louise Quinn.

The letter includes a statement from Shamrock Rovers captain and Professional Footballers’ Association of Ireland (PFA) chair, Roberto Lopes.

International rights organisations have also called on UEFA and FIFA to exclude Israel from its competitions.

“It’s unconscionable that Israel will participate despite clear evidence that Israel’s football association continues to support illegal settlements,” Amnesty International said in a statement.

“When rules are broken, when occupation, apartheid and genocide are ongoing, we cannot look the other way,” it added.

What have Ireland’s officials said about the match?

Ireland’s Prime Minister Micheal Martin gave a green light to the matches, citing the challenges of mixing sport and politics.

“We have been critics and have opposed very strongly Israeli government policy within Gaza in particular. We condemned the Hamas attack on Israel, which was absolutely horrific,” ‌‌the PM or taoiseach told The Irish Times.

“I think sport is an area that can be challenging when it crosses into the realm of politics.”

In February, FAI Chief Executive David Courell said the national team had no choice but ‌‌to ‌‌fulfil its obligations or risk harming the long-term sporting interests of Irish football, including potential disqualification from future competitions.

Last week, Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson responded to the boycott calls, saying his team were not “playing with genocide”.

“We’re playing against genocide,” Hallgrimsson said.

What is the public sentiment in Ireland?

The rights groups calling for a boycott of the match have cited several public polls, run by local newspapers, footballers’ bodies and individuals online, which indicate that a vast majority are in favour of opting out of the Nations League fixtures.

A poll by the PFA in February showed that 63 percent of those surveyed did not want Ireland to play the fixtures. A similar poll by the Irish Mirror newspaper indicated that 71 percent of the public would support the FAI if they refused to play the game.

Bohemian FC, an Irish football club with a strong pro-Palestine stance, have thrown their weight behind the calls for a boycott and have urged the FAI to call off their participation.

Bohemian’s Director of Football Pat Fenlon believes it is up to the FAI to “take a stand for what’s happening in Gaza”.

“What an opportunity it would be to be the first country to stand up and say this is totally wrong,” Fenlon told Irish Sport for Palestine.

“The game shouldn’t be played,” he said.

According to officials at the club, the Irish public is aware of the potential consequences, but believe that boycotting is “the right thing to do”.

“It is not acceptable to put a price on standing up for what is right and in solidarity with the Palestinian people,” the club’s communications director Luke O’Rodrian told Al Jazeera.

He accused the FAI of showing “sheer cowardice”.

O’Rodrian said the boycott calls have been supported by trade unions representing workers, particularly those employed by the FAI, the PFA and the Irish Football Supporters Partnership, who represent Ireland’s football supporters.

In the country’s political sphere, Mary Lou McDonald, leader of Ireland’s main opposition party, Sinn Fein, has also called for the FAI to “do the right thing by its players” by telling them not to take the field.

The Israeli FA responded to Hallgrimsson’s statement on Monday by saying: “We are not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity; we’re playing against the coach who embodies them”.

Martin defended Hallgrimsson, describing Israel’s remarks as “unacceptable”, adding that “Israel can’t keep denying what the world knows”.

Why are the matches being played in Hungary and Serbia?

The first leg of the fixture will be held at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen, Hungary, and the second, which is Ireland’s “home” game, will be played at the TSC Arena in Backa Topola, Serbia.

Israel has not played an international fixture at home since September 2023, as it has been barred by UEFA from hosting teams due to security concerns.

While the October 4 fixture was scheduled to be held in Dublin, the FAI moved it following the protests and boycott calls. That game will be played behind closed doors.

Irish state broadcaster RTE, which ‌‌has ‌‌contractual obligations to show the games, will provide stripped-back coverage.

There will be no studio presentation or punditry, and commentary will be taken from the international feed. RTE has not taken advertising or sponsorship around either game.

What would happen if Ireland boycotted the match?

UEFA does not have a fixed fine for refusing to play a Nations League match, and forfeiting teams could face a mix of fines, point penalties and forfeitures.

Officials at Bohemian FC pointed towards a recent report in the Irish Examiner newspaper, which highlighted that the punishment given to Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia when they refused to fulfil recent UEFA fixtures against Belarus was a 3-0 walkover and, in one case, a fine of 5,000 euros ($5,684).

O’Rodrian said there was “real anger” among grassroots towards the FAI.

“The FAI exaggerated the potential consequences to force their delegates to vote in favour of proceeding with fulfilling these fixtures,” he said.

Meanwhile, Bohemians’ Director of Football Fenlon believed such a stance would always come at a cost.

“[They are] talking about losing money, about losing points and punishment, but we’re talking about more than 20,000 children killed [in Gaza],” he said.

“There will be a cost. Stand on the right side. We shouldn’t be playing Israel in anything.”

articles.title: Graham Alexander: Bradford City 'reluctantly' give Preston North End permission to speak to boss
articles.summary: Bradford City "reluctantly" give Championship strugglers Preston permission to speak to boss Graham Alexander about their managerial vacancy.
articles.body:
Bradford City have "reluctantly" given Championship strugglers Preston North End permission to speak to boss Graham Alexander about their managerial vacancy.

Paul Heckingbottom was sacked after two years in charge of North End earlier this month following six defeats in their opening seven league games.

Alexander, 54, had two spells at Deepdale as a player and made 372 league appearances for the club.

He had a five-game spell in caretaker charge in 2011-12 before ending his playing career with the Lilywhites at the end of that season, aged 40.

"Bradford City AFC can confirm we have been approached by Preston North End to speak to Graham Alexander regarding the Championship side's managerial vacancy," the Bantams said in a statement. , external

"Reluctantly, Bradford City has granted permission for Graham to speak to Preston North End."

BBC Radio Lancashire reports that Preston are down to their final two candidates for the role.

The Bantams are top of League One with five wins from their first seven games of the season.

Alexander took over at Valley Parade in November 2023 and led them to promotion from League Two in his first full season in charge.

They finished fourth in League One in 2025-26 before losing to Bolton Wanderers in the play-offs.

The former Scotland international, who has also had spells in charge of Fleetwood, Scunthorpe, Salford, Motherwell and MK Dons, is contracted to the club until the end of next season.

Preston are second bottom of the Championship with four points from eight matches and host Millwall in their first game after the international break on Saturday, 10 October.

articles.title: Figo: "No creo que los árbitros estén contra el Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: El luso y Guti se mojan en el torneo benéfico de golf de La Herrería organizado por Clínica Menorca
articles.summary: El luso y Guti se mojan en el torneo benéfico de golf de La Herrería organizado por Clínica Menorca
articles.body: Muchas caras conocidas en San Lorenzo de El Escorial con motivo del XXV torneo benéfico de golf en el club de La Herrería organizado por Clínica Menorca para recaudar fondos en la lucha contra el cáncer de mama. Luis Figo y Guti, que abordaron todo lo que ha dejado el último derbi, el alcalde José Luis Martínez Almeida, Raúl González, Pavón, la ex presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid Esperanza Aguirre, Feliciano López, entre otras caras conocidas, participaron en este torneo. Los fondos recaudados para este torneo han servido también para recaudar 5.000 euros que ayudarán a impulsar, a través de la Fundación La Sonrisa de María, la investigación del sarcoma de Ewing y a las familias que tienen que enfrentarse a esta enfermedad. Otros 8.000 han ido a parar a la Fundación MD Anderson contra el cáncer de mama. Antes del torneo, algunos de los protagonistas atendieron a los medios de comunicación. El derbi aún colea, sobre todo por las quejas del Madrid, y Luis Figo, uno de los habituales a este torneo, dio su punto de vista. "Luis, ¿crees que los árbitros van contra el Madrid?", le preguntaron al luso. "Uno cuando pierde siempre está enfadado, pero no creo eso. Al final, los equipos grandes siempre salen beneficiados, si contamos todo a la temporada. Al Madrid le veo bien. Nuevo entrenador, pues nueva ilusión para la afición, para el club. Ha tenido algún partido que no ha podido ganar, pero es larga la temporada y yo creo que al final es una competición de regularidad". Sobre el Balón de Oro, no ve un claro favorito. "Yo no voto, hay una serie de candidatos que pueden ganar. Hay que decir que no es la UEFA, aunque ya lo sabéis, y es complicado decir. Entre algún jugador español que ganó el Mundial, alguno que ganó la Champions con el PSG o Mbappé, que hizo una gran temporada", añadió Figo, que habla de que algunos de los candidatos pidan el voto. "Yo tenía que haber pedido más para mí (bromea). Ahora es distinto, las cosas han cambiado, antes no hacíamos tanta campaña para ganarlo". Por su parte, Guti sí tiene un preferido para el Balón de Oro. "Yo creo que va a estar entre Harry Kane, Mbappé y Rodri. Está muy dividido Yo quiero que lo gané en Mbappé porque juega en el Madrid. El Mundial lo ha ganado Fabian y ha ganado la Champions, pero no creo que se lo vayan a dar a Fabian. Fabian no tiene ese nombre como para ganar un Balón de Oro, que seguramente, que si es por méritos, lo tendría que ganar, pero hay otros que tienen más nombre". No ve Guti un problema que Rodri no haya fichado por el Madrid. "Me hubiera gustado que viniera, pero a final es una decisión suya y, bueno, seguro que está contento en el Barcelona, pero creo que el Madrid tiene un gran equipo y no creo que vaya a echar de menos a Rodri". Del derbi, Guti piensa como Figo: "No creo que los árbitros vayan contra el Madrid, pero en el derbi hubo decisiones como para estar enfadado. Cualquier entrenador se habría quejado, no solo Mourinho". José Luis Martínez Almeida llegó sonriente a La Herrería después del triunfo de su Atlético. Al alcalde le preguntaron por la guerra abierta entre Florentino Pérez y Javier Tebas. "Lo que a mí parece es a la prensa el salseo le viene muy bien ahora que hay tres semanas sin fútbol. Es difícil que me pueda meter ahí y mira que me gusta meterme en charcos. Pero tampoco sé exactamente lo que reclama el Madrid, lo que dice la Liga... Lo único que puedo decir es esta liga es la mejor del mundo y en parte es gracias a que está el Madrid, así que a disfrutarlo". Del derbi, se mojó con las decisiones tan polémicas del derbi. "Me parece que la entrada de Kang in Lee es roja pero la del Cuti Romero no. Y creo que el Atlético fue mejor. Era penalti claro a Giuliano y nadie lo discutió. A veces me benefician y otras me perjudican. En cuanto a Mourinho juega muy bien el otro fútbol y lo hace bien además".

articles.title: Britain has banned beer in soccer stands for over 40 years. Is that about to change?
articles.summary: Alcohol has been banned in the stands of British soccer games for over 40 years, but UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened the door for the law to be repealed, saying he thinks it’s “discriminatory.”
articles.body: Note: This story first appeared in The Beautiful Game by CNN Sports, our biweekly newsletter on all things global soccer – men’s and women’s. To subscribe, click here. Hello everyone, Spanish Editor Patrick here. Ben is enjoying a well-earned mini-vacation on the Emerald Isle, hence I am taking the reins for one edition so that Mr. Church can enjoy as many stouts and joyous conversations as Ireland can offer up before he returns on Monday. Sláinte to you, pal. In today’s edition of the newsletter, we will be looking at the somewhat quick return of our dear old friend International Soccer – we thought we left you behind for a while after the World Cup, but somehow, you’re back. We’ll also take a look at an ugly incident that shows women still have to fight for their place in soccer, hear from Kylian Mbappé on his chances for the Ballon d’Or, look at the North Korean under-20 women’s team, and we’re debuting a new recurring segment – with your help – about why you love your soccer club. Anyways, plenty to get into today, but let’s begin with something that’s become a talker here in the UK: Will fans be able to drink beer in stadiums again? The Main Thing: Can Brits drink beer in the stands once again? If you’re reading from the US, you might be shocked to find out that you can’t drink beer in the stands at soccer matches in a few big leagues across Europe (e.g. Spain’s La Liga, France’s Ligue 1 and England’s Premier League), but that might soon be changing in the United Kingdom if the prime minister has his way. UK PM Andy Burnham recently told reporters that he felt the current laws on the books banning alcohol in the stands at the top five tiers in the English game were “discriminatory” in nature, given that fans can drink in many of the other spectator sports in the country (rugby, tennis and cricket, for example). “I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out,” Burnham said while at the United Nations in New York, according to the BBC. “I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different. “And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done. It could happen on a trial basis.” The legislation Burnham refers to – the Sporting Events Act 1985 – was introduced by Margaret Thatcher’s government to help combat violence around the game in England and Wales. The home secretary at the time said alcohol was a “major contributory factor in violent and disorderly behavior,” so the ban was introduced. While hooliganism and fan violence were a big issue in the 1980s and 90s, incidents gradually declined until today where English fans largely have a much better reputation abroad. Burnham might face some difficulties in repealing or altering the law though given the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPC) told the BBC that any changes would mean “challenges” to the “safety of staff and fans at football games” and to police work. The UKFPC added that soccer matches see far more “violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters” compared to other sports. “It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games,” it concluded. Still, a lot of support for a repeal is arising from certain circles, with the Football Supporters’ Association calling the Sports Events Act of 1985 “outdated,” with its president Tom Greatrex saying, “We welcome the prime minister’s comments and totally agree that the legislation … deserves to be reviewed.” Beer is currently allowed to be sold in England’s Women’s Super League following successful trials in its competitions, so the precedent is there, but it remains to be seen how far this will go given there does not appear to be any official movement to change the law. I guess it’s still off to the pubs (shoutout to the Salmon and Ball in Bethnal Green) before kickoffs. Quote of the week These are the words of North Korea’s under-20 midfielder Choe Rim-jong after securing a ticket to the U20 Women’s World Cup final against Spain. It might be a surprise to some, given the Asian nation’s reclusive nature, but North Korea is a women’s soccer powerhouse, particularly on the junior level. North Korea is the defending champion and has won three U20 Women’s World Cups in total, also finishing runner-up once in 2008. Oddly, the senior team’s best finish at a Women’s World Cup is the quarterfinals in 2007. Now, after a 3-0 victory over Colombia in the semifinals, the under-20s are back in the final, ready to reign supreme over the junior levels in the hope of a better senior run next year at the World Cup in Brazil. Columbus Crew reserve team coach fired after incident involving ‘physical abuse and sexism’ While we are witnessing big growth in both the quality and interest in the women’s game, we unfortunately are still experiencing some events that are holding women’s participation in the Beautiful Game back. Major League Soccer (MLS) team Columbus Crew fired Federico Higuaín, the head coach of their reserve team, following an incident in a game that a referees’ association deemed “physical abuse and sexism” toward a female referee. Higuaín – who was appointed head coach of the franchise’s reserve squad, Crew 2, in January 2025 – squeezed and refused to let go of a female referee’s hand during a recent MLS NEXT Pro match and told the official, “Don’t forget this is a man’s game.” MLS NEXT Pro subsequently investigated the incident and suspended Higuaín for two matches before the Crew let him go. Read the full story here. WATCH: Kylian Mbappé on the Ballon d’Or – ‘It can be a good year for me’ Kylian Mbappé fell short of winning the World Cup in the summer, and he – quite annoyingly for me as a madridista – failed to win anything with Real Madrid last year, too, so many might be asking why he deserves to win the Ballon d’Or. Well, he sat down with CNN Sports’ Amanda Davies to make his argument for why he should win soccer’s most prestigious individual award, saying that the prize should go to the best individual player in the world. Click the video above or here to watch. Also if you want to read all about what Mbappé had to tell CNN Sports (or watch the full interview), click here. What to watch New CNN Sports intern Fraser Godden has compiled a couple of men’s internationals you should watch over the weekend. Men’s UEFA Nations League, Group A3: England vs. Spain When? Saturday – 2:45 p.m. ET / 7:45 p.m. local time Where? Wembley Stadium, London, England World champion Spain might have hoped for an easier return to international soccer to celebrate its World Cup triumph against Argentina just two months ago. Instead, La Roja visits Wembley to take on England in a repeat of the Euro 2024 final, which Spain won 2-1. Fans will be hoping for a match that closer reflects the 2026 Bronze Medal match rather than the final given the 6-4 goalfest that played out between the Three Lions and France in Miami. England manager Thomas Tuchel selected a 27-man squad for the upcoming fixtures against Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia but has been rocked by withdrawals from Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Declan Rice, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo. La Roja – looking to extend its record-breaking 38-match unbeaten run in competitive fixtures – called up stars Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres but will be without full-back Pedro Porro through injury. (Spanish editor’s note: Fraser will be on site Saturday to capture some color for Monday’s newsletter, so stay tuned.) Men’s International Friendlies: USMNT vs. Peru When? Saturday – 4:30 p.m. ET (local time) Where? Inter.co Stadium, Orlando, Florida, United States The US Men’s National Team (USMNT) returns to the field following its heartbreaking World Cup loss to Belgium in the round of 16, taking on Peru in Orlando with the next generation very much the focus of the camp. Mauricio Pochettino’s men will take on the 50th-ranked nation with a fresh squad after the Argentine boss selected 13 uncapped players and eight teenagers – including 16-year-old Philadelphia Union sensation Cavan Sullivan – for the matches against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. The squad is bolstered by call ups for experienced players, such as Tyler Adams and Antonee Robinson, but finds itself without Ricardo Pepi through injury and with some relatively shocking omissions (Christian Pulisic and World Cup hero Folarin Balogun are also out). Only Gio Reyna has scored 10 or more goals in the squad, so this definitely looks like experimentation time for Pochettino. Why I love my club: Ayr United New to soccer fandom? Well, those match recommendations above should help to find out what to watch and why, but if you are a long-time fan (or jumped into the game fervently just recently), you likely have a favorite club that you will watch no matter what, even if you know it’s likely to end in frustration or numbness. Today, we begin a new segment on the soccer love of your life with intrepid intern Fraser, who is a die-hard fan of a Scottish team you have likely never heard of. It’s highly irregular for a born and bred Glaswegian to not support one of the two big teams in Scotland, such has been the dominance of Celtic and Rangers in Scottish soccer. Yes, they’re giants of the game and enjoy regular, if not constant, success – but where’s the fun in that? My love for Ayr United in the second-tier Scottish Championship is far more exhilarating, in my opinion, and is something that will never be broken. I’ve invested far too much time and emotions in my “wee” team from the Ayrshire coast. My connection with “The Honest Men” – inspired by Ayrshire’s own Robert Burns’ famous poem, “Tam O’Shanter” – goes back long before I can remember. Before I could protest, I was wrapped in a black-and-white babygrow by my Ayr United-obsessed father. And that was that. From that point on, it was part of my identity, whether I liked it or not. Every other Saturday in my childhood involved trips down to Somerset Park on the train to watch part-time soccer players battle the unforgiving wind and rain of the west coast of Scotland. I loved it. At that time, Ayr bounced between the second and third tiers of Scottish soccer and the thrill of a promotion or relegation battle from one season to the next drew me in from an early age. Admittedly, supporting a small team had its difficulties as a youngster. “Why support them if they’re rubbish?” or “When was the last time they won anything?” were standard responses to my declaration of love for Ayr. But that made me defiant. The day Ayr qualifies for the Champions League will taste even sweeter, let me tell you. Just look at Bodø/Glimt. If that squad can do it, why can’t ours? Since attending my first match as a three-year-old, I’ve enjoyed the highest of highs – winning League One on the final day and reaching the semifinal of the League Cup and earning a trip to Hampden to play our bitter rival – and endured the lowest of lows (losing to our bitter rival at Hampden in said League Cup semifinal). But that’s why I love my club. There truly is no greater feeling than standing on the old-style terracing at Somerset Park with the wind battering my face while Ayr United plays the Beautiful Game. Are you a huge fan of a soccer club? Do you have heartbreaking tales and glorious triumphs or experiences to share? Well, send us your story and we could feature you in a future edition of The Beautiful Game. The Final Whistle: Why do we have such a long international break this time around? If it seems like the international break has rushed up on us quite suddenly, it’s probably because it has. The World Cup wrapped up on July 19 and the Premier League kicked off just over a month later. As fans were just beginning to digest the celebrated return of the club game, the break for national teams pressed pause on domestic leagues roughly five weeks after they began, with Germany’s Bundesliga playing just four games and both France’s Ligue 1 and the Premier League five each – quite a paltry offering for club-soccer starved fans. Additionally, the break is three weeks long as opposed to the usual two. Why though? Well, it’s actually probably a good thing they did it. The FIFA Council approved the lengthened break in March 2023 as part of its plan to rejig its international calendar and lessen disruptions to domestic leagues following the newly-expanded World Cup this year. The result is that, instead of three international breaks in the first half of the club season, we now have two. Also, the total number of weeks club seasons will be paused is five as opposed to six. The idea, ironically, is to allow the players more rest as they won’t have to fly around the world as many weeks (e.g. an Asian or South American player on a European team would likely face brutal travel schedules). The result means an extended three-week first international break that allows teams to play up to four matches, which we are now beginning. So what to make of it all? I’m not sure really. If you like international soccer like me, it’s not too bad, but if you miss the domestic club game, this is likely going to be a rough three weeks – though you (and the players) will suffer less in the long run.

articles.title: La afición del Rayo anuncia una demanda contra el club por los partidos en Butarque
articles.standfirst: Reclama la devolución de la parte proporcional del abono correspondiente a los tres partidos jugados como local en Leganés
articles.summary: Reclama la devolución de la parte proporcional del abono correspondiente a los tres partidos jugados como local en Leganés
articles.body: La Plataforma ADRV, que engloba a la gran mayoría de peñas del Rayo, ha anunciado que interpondrá una demanda judicial conjunta contra el Rayo Vallecano para reclamar la devolución de la parte proporcional del abono correspondiente a los partidos que el conjunto franjirrojo ha disputado como local en el Estadio de Butarque, en Leganés. El procedimiento judicial lo llevará a cabo el abogado Javier Flores con todas las solicitudes de los aficionados del Rayo Vallecano que quieran ejercer una reclamación económica por el perjuicio ocasionado debido al cierre del Estadio de Vallecas. En su comunicado, la Plataforma ADRV recuerda que el Rayo abrió el pasado 24 de julio la campaña de abonados para la temporada 2026-2027 mientras todavía tenía pendiente de resolver un requerimiento de la Comunidad de Madrid relacionado con la seguridad y el mantenimiento del Estadio de Vallecas. Cuatro días después, el 28 de julio, la Comunidad acordó la suspensión cautelar de la concesión del estadio y posteriormente abrió un procedimiento para la extinción definitiva de dicha concesión, obligando al Rayo a disputar sus partidos como local en otro emplazamiento. El lugar elegido fue Butarque, donde el equipo disputó los encuentros frente al Alavés, Real Racing Club de Santander y Espanyol, tres partidos que estaban inicialmente incluidos en los abonos de la temporada. "Durante todo este proceso, los abonados hemos sido los grandes olvidados. No hemos recibido una disculpa pública ni una sola explicación. Hemos tenido que acudir a taquillas con plazos irrisorios y hemos sido utilizados como arma arrojadiza en un conflicto que no provocamos. Es, una vez más, la forma en que esta directiva trata a su afición. Tampoco hemos recibido compensación alguna por la parte proporcional del abono correspondiente a los partidos que no pudimos disfrutar en nuestro estadio", exponen los aficionados en su comunicado. La Plataforma ADRV asegura que la compensación les "corresponde por lo que establecen las condiciones de la campaña de abonos 2026-2027 y por la Ley 17/1997, de Espectáculos Públicos y Actividades Recreativas de la Comunidad de Madrid".

articles.title: Koke, capitán récord a récord
articles.standfirst: Entre los innumerables hitos del jugador que más veces ha vestido la rojiblanca está ser el que más derbis ha ganado con el Atlético : 14 duelos
articles.summary: Entre los innumerables hitos del jugador que más veces ha vestido la rojiblanca está ser el que más derbis ha ganado con el Atlético : 14 duelos
articles.body: De profesión: capitán. Y los récords. Porque eso acumula Jorge Resurrección, Koke para el fútbol, en su inmaculada trayectoria desde que debutó hace más de 17 años en el primer equipo del Atlético, club en el que ha forjado una leyenda con cifras que pasarán muchos años para ser igualadas. Si es que alguien lo consigue. Para empezar, la última hazaña pasa por convertirse el pasado domingo en el jugador con más victorias ante el Madrid: 14 son las ocasiones en las que ha derrotado a los blancos, algo jamás logrado por otro rojiblanco. Como tampoco disputar 28 derbis solo en un campeonato de Liga que ha conquistado dos veces (el único de toda la plantilla). Dos títulos que se entienden por el hecho de haber batido otro récord, el de temporadas en el primer equipo. Con la actual, son ya 18 las que ha defendido la elástica rojiblanca y a una caseta en la que es el primer capitán desde el 2019 (año de la marcha de Diego Godín). Obviamente, también es el que más partidos ha sudado la rojiblanca, con 748. Una marca que batió hace varias temporadas y donde casi ya lleva más de 200 encuentros más que el anterior jugador que tenía la plusmarca, el legendario Adelardo. También, claro, es el que más minutos ha jugado. Sus 56.307 minutos no encuentran parangón en la historia de una entidad que ya supera los 123 años de historia. Tampoco lo hacen las 111 asistencias que ha brindado a sus compañeros pese a que durante muchos cursos se ha desempeñado como mediocentro. Todos estos números explican la leyenda Koke, el capitán récord a récord que tiene contrato hasta el 30 de junio de 2027 pero que no ha perdido su vigencia en el equipo. En el derbi, día señalado, recibió los elogios en forma de suspiros de un Simeone que sabe que, al igual que con Griezmann, será difícil encontrar otro como Koke. Enumerados sus registros más importantes, hay uno que se le resiste y que intentará conseguir esta temporada. Hablamos de los títulos, donde lleva ocho y está a dos del citado Adelardo. Son cuatro los entorchados que peleará el Atleti este curso y las opciones de Koke de hacerse con el que sería el mejor colofón a su brillante carrera. De momento, mantener su versión del derbi (dio 62 pases buenos de 64 y generó más ocasiones que nadie, tres) acercaría a los de Simeone a volver a tocar metal después de aquella Liga 20-21 que levantó Koke como su primer y último título de capitán.
